results.content: Therefore, we simulated planned incomplete data and compared the computational accuracy (bias of point estimates, bias of variability estimates, root mean squared error, and coverage rates) and computational feasibility (convergence rates and estimation time) of three recently proposed estimation methods for ICCs: Markov chain Monte Carlo estimation of Bayesian hierarchical linear models, maximum likelihood estimation of random-effects models, and maximum likelihood estimation of common-factor models. For observational studies with a PMD, standard software based on the random-effects ANOVA model cannot provide least-squares estimates of variance components or ICCs. Brennan (Citation2001, Chapter 7) mentioned analogous-ANOVA methods such as Henderson’s (Citation1953) Methods 1 and 3 and MINQUE (Hartley et al., Citation1978) as possible solutions for estimating variance components under unbalanced designs. Given current methodological knowledge and software availability, we found the MLE-RE method the single preferred method to estimate ICCs for IRR for differing sample sizes of subjects and raters, magnitudes of raters variance, and across proportions of missing observations.
